text:
marie: quick heads-up — we started the zodiac15b int4 canary overnight and the perf tail ballooned. p50 ~90ms -> 125ms, p95 ~200ms -> ~460ms. also a few long-summary hallucinations cropped up in the QA set.

dan: thanks. was this with the same microbatch/batch_window used in fp16 runs?

marie: yes, microbatch=8, batch_window=12ms. throughput down ~20%. memory fragmentation metric (slab_free_list thrash) is much higher during long responses.

tariq: what's the quant recipe? per-channel or per-tensor, symmetric/asymmetric?

marie: 4-bit asymmetric per-tensor with stock folding from the last quant rollout.

olivia: are the hallucinations correlated with token length? any particular max_new_tokens set for the run?

marie: max_new_tokens was 1024 (our model default). the bad outputs are from prompts that generate 700-900 tokens.

dan: int4 kernels plus large KV prefetch could be stomping allocator. Any slab traces?

marie: dropping a snippet from the node:

```
2026-03-22T22:14:05Z decode_peak_alloc=13.1GB
2026-03-22T22:14:05Z kv_prefetch start session=0a5c...
2026-03-22T22:14:06Z slab_free_list thrash +900
2026-03-22T22:14:06Z p95 spike observed
```

tariq: looks like classic frag pattern. two-pronged short-term: 1) lower max_new_tokens default for zodiac15b to 256 2) reduce batch_window 12ms -> 8ms to reduce large coalesced batches

olivia: also propose enabling a 1.2GB warmup cushion on the canary hosts to keep freelists primed. we used that before for another 13b model and it reduced thrash.

dan: additional safety: roll back a small % to int8 kernel to see if tails are kernel-related or quantization-related.

marie: plan sounds solid. I'll create a canary patch: - model.default.max_new_tokens=256 - batch_window_ms=8 - warmup_cushion_gb=1.2 - canary split: 12% int8, 88% int4.

infra-bot: created canary patch canary/1747654322-quick-tail-mitigations, targets 4 nodes, 15% traffic. Deploy queued.

olivia: I'll run the QA harness (rouge/bleu/precision@k and hallucination detector) across int4 and int8 lanes once live.

dan: if int8 shows better tail but similar median, then int4 kernels likely causing scheduling or allocator contention. if both degrade, it's probably quantization quality.

marie: starting deployment. early readout after 30m: p50 improved to ~98ms, p95 ~240ms on patched nodes. workload still noisy, running 6h perf + 24h QA.

olivia: thanks — when QA finishes, post the diff and a few example failures. also file a follow-up to add per-model "safe_max_new_tokens" in model metadata and a playbook entry for int4 rollouts.

dan: one more note: consider limiting KV prefetch to only prefetch for sequences >512 tokens to avoid prefetch churn on mixed-length fleets.

marie: noted. will add prefetch_threshold_tokens=512 to the patch in next iteration if current mitigations don't fully fix the tail.

infra-bot: canary deploy started :rocket: patch id canary/1747654322-quick-tail-mitigations

marie: will report back with full artifacts and QA diffs. early signs promising but not yet green.
